variant_perception_summary: Two offsetting mispriced-in-opposite-directions reads, neither dominant enough for high conviction: underlying demand (Gross Bookings +24% cc) may be under-credited because reported revenue growth looks like it decelerated when most of that is a one-time UK accounting reclassification; simultaneously, the 4-quarter EBITDA guidance-beat streak the market implicitly trusts likely still nets a recurring 'one-off' legal-reserve add-back (17.3%/6.5% of Adjusted EBITDA) that the company stopped reconciling to GAAP starting Q1 FY2026.
what_everyone_knows: Uber is the largest, most profitable ride-hailing/delivery platform, growing Gross Bookings above 20% for four straight quarters, and is buying Delivery Hero in the biggest deal in its history.
what_is_priced_in: A slowing, not accelerating, growth story — the market prices just a 5.05% ten-year FCF growth rate (reverse-DCF) and a 10.78% steady-state margin Uber has already beaten on a trailing basis (12.13% TTM EBIT margin); revenue consensus has also been cut 1.04% in the 3 trading days after the Q2 print.
what_market_may_be_missing: The reported revenue deceleration (18%→12.2%) is substantially a one-time UK accounting reclassification, not weaker demand, and the market may be under-crediting genuine ~20-25% underlying growth — but at the same time the 'clean 4-quarter beat streak' narrative likely still nets a recurring 'one-off' legal-reserve add-back the company stopped reconciling to GAAP, a real quality gap the beat-streak story does not price.
edge_proof: Q3 FY2026 print (Nov-03-2026) shows a genuine, ex-UK cost-of-revenue improvement without a legal-accrual reversal, AND the FY2026 10-K restores the full Adjusted-EBITDA-to-GAAP reconciliation — checkable within roughly six months.
killer_risk: The derivative lawsuit surviving a motion to dismiss with discovery corroborating the board's proxy statements were false — converting an unproven allegation into a proven integrity finding — landing at the same time the €14.2bn Delivery Hero bridge is drawn in full on undisclosed, possibly rich, terms.

red_flags.description: Unresolved federal shareholder derivative lawsuit naming CEO, Chairman, and every sitting director, alleging suppressed safety data and false 2024-2026 proxy disclosures on board safety oversight. Unproven (confidence 2/5, web-sourced only).
Serial-acquirer / debt-funded M&A pattern: Careem sold to minority (2023) then re-bought to control (2026); pending $14.8bn debt-funded Delivery Hero takeover, bridge ~1.2x pre-deal total debt.
Discontinuation of the company-level Adjusted-EBITDA-to-GAAP reconciliation, effective Q1 FY2026, unacknowledged on either subsequent earnings call.
Recurring 'legal, non-income tax, and regulatory reserve' line added back to Adjusted EBITDA as non-recurring in both FY2024 ($1,123M) and FY2025 ($564M).
Drizly ($1.1bn alcohol-delivery acquisition, closed Oct-2021) shut down entirely ~2.5 years after close — full write-off.
Two adjudicated MDL jury verdicts (Arizona $8.5mm Feb-2026; Charlotte NC $5,000 Apr-2026) not named in the three most recent filings despite an aggregate litigation reserve being disclosed.
Fast-changing industry / rate-of-change risk (score 32/100, ≤40 threshold): unresolved autonomous-vehicle transition where Waymo already operates an independent commercialized fleet.

Aggressive accounting practice pattern: recurring 'non-recurring' legal/regulatory reserve line (17.3% FY24 / 6.5% FY25 of Adjusted EBITDA), discontinued GAAP reconciliation, and a +162% (3-year) self-insurance reserve build driving part of reported OCF growth.
